title: Evaluation at an initial object into a left fibration is a trivial Kan fibration
statement: Use quasicategories, initial objects and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and trivial Kan fibrations of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Fix a universe containing left fibrations $p:D\to B$ and $q:T\to B$ of quasicategories, and an initial object $d\in D$. Put $b=p(d)$ and $T_b=T\times_B\{b\}$. Define $\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(D,T)_n$ to consist of simplicial maps $H:D\times\Delta^n\to T$ with $qH=p\operatorname{pr}_D$, with operators given by restriction in the second factor. Then restriction to $\{d\}\times\Delta^n$ defines a trivial Kan fibration $\operatorname{ev}_d:\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(D,T)\to T_b$. Thus evaluation is surjective on vertices and has the right lifting property against every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, including $n=0$. No initial object is required in $T$; $T$ and $T_b$ may be empty.

source.place: Proposition 5.6.6.19, implication (2) => (3), read online 2026-10-17; Kerodon tag, not Stacks tag; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Use the opposite simplicial set defined in clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]: an operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ is replaced by $\alpha^r(a)=n-\alpha(m-a)$. That clause makes $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ a quasicategory and gives $\operatorname{Map}_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,d)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_D(d,x)$. The latter spaces are weakly contractible because $d$ is initial, in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Hence [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-anodyne], with $J=D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $t=d$, makes $j:\{d\}\hookrightarrow D^{\mathrm{op}}$ right anodyne.

source.place: Corollary 4.7.3.22, final-object implication (1) => (3), applied to the opposite quasicategory; the cited opposite-mapping-space comparison supplies its hypothesis.

proof.text: Order reversal takes $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. Since $0<k\leq n$ implies $0\leq n-k<n$, any right-horn lifting square for $q^{\mathrm{op}}:T^{\mathrm{op}}\to B^{\mathrm{op}}$ becomes a left-horn lifting square for $q$; [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] supplies a filler, whose opposite fills the original square. Thus $q^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a right fibration. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] to $q^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the right-anodyne $j$ of step 1. It gives a trivial Kan fibration $\rho^r:\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},T^{\mathrm{op}})\to\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},B^{\mathrm{op}})\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(\{d\},B^{\mathrm{op}})}\operatorname{Fun}(\{d\},T^{\mathrm{op}})$. All these simplicial sets lie in the fixed universe.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4, right-fibration/right-anodyne clause; explicit reversal of the left-fibration horn condition.

proof.text: For any $H:K\times\Delta^n\to X$, take its opposite and precompose in the second factor with $r_n:\Delta^n\cong(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$, which sends a monotone $\beta:[m]\to[n]$ to $a\mapsto n-\beta(m-a)$. This gives the degree-$n$ bijection $\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},X^{\mathrm{op}})$: reversing twice is the inverse, and the formula for $\alpha^r$ in step 1 verifies the simplicial operators from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The formula commutes with composition in $X$ and restriction in $K$, so the map $\rho^r$ of step 2 is the opposite of $\rho:\operatorname{Fun}(D,T)\to Y=\operatorname{Fun}(D,B)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(\{d\},B)}\operatorname{Fun}(\{d\},T)$. Reversal preserves the boundary, since it permutes vertices and thus preserves non-surjectivity of simplex maps. Consequently a boundary lifting square for $\rho$ reverses to one for $\rho^r$; reverse its filler to obtain a filler for the original square. The degree-zero bijections also give vertex surjectivity of $\rho$. By [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], $\rho$ is a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4, elementary passage from the right-fibration result to the left-fibration result using explicit order reversal and the internal-functor definition.

proof.text: Define $\iota:T_b\to Y$ in degree $n$ by $t:\Delta^n\to T_b\mapsto(p\operatorname{pr}_D,t)$, viewing $t$ as a map $\{d\}\times\Delta^n\to T$. This pair belongs to $Y_n$ because $qt$ is constant at $b=p(d)$. The degreewise pullback of $\rho$ along $\iota$ consists of pairs $(H,t)$ with $qH=p\operatorname{pr}_D$ and $H|_{\{d\}\times\Delta^n}=t$; eliminating the uniquely determined $t$ identifies it with the stated $\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(D,T)$ and its projection with $\operatorname{ev}_d$. For a boundary square for this projection, compose its bottom map with $\iota$ and lift against $\rho$ using step 3. The equality of its image with $\iota(t)$ forces $qH=p\operatorname{pr}_D$ and the prescribed evaluation, so the filler lies in this pullback. For $n=0$, vertex surjectivity of $\rho$ lifts $\iota(t)$ and the same equalities put its lift in the pullback. These are exactly the surjectivity and boundary clauses of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration].

lean.statement: theorem initialEvaluationTrivialKanFibration {D B T : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory D] [Quasicategory B] [Quasicategory T] (p : D ⟶ B) (q : T ⟶ B) (hp : leftFibration p) (hq : leftFibration q) (d : D _⦋0⦌) (hd : IsInitial D d) : ∃ ev : fiber ((ihom D).map q) (diagramVertex p) ⟶ fiber q (p.app _ d), ev ≫ pullback.snd (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) (p.app _ d)) q = pullback.snd (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) (diagramVertex p)) ((ihom D).map q) ≫ evaluation D T d ∧ SSet.modelCategoryQuillen.I.rlp ev
lean.note: Uses the existing strict fiber of the internal-hom postcomposition map to express Fun over B. The projection equation uniquely fixes the canonical evaluation map, so the existential is not an arbitrary trivial Kan fibration. No new definition or dependency needed.
